facts.fact: The Interior Ministry says ID for D will cover all layers of civil status, with births taken at health facilities or by the civil-status officer feeding a unique ID number, and an interoperability link between public services; planned, preliminary scope eleven communes.

BDI.note: Nothing stated on the central bank.
Only a presidential recommendation that civil-status services be digitalised; no system procured or piloted.
Nothing stated on civil servant training.
Nothing stated on government payments to people.
No enrolment count or share given.

facts.fact: Permanent secretary Valentin Nahimana of the Interior Ministry says a unique identification number with fingerprints will be given to each child at birth, in a health facility or before the civil-status officer, under the ID for D project; a plan, preliminary scope eleven communes.

BDI.note: Nothing stated on who operates or owns the ID system.
Only a general interoperability link between public services; no register named as keyed on the ID number.
A diagnostic study and a planned biometric card; no system procured, built or piloted is stated.
Nothing stated on local government office connection.
No local civil registration office system stated as built or in use.

facts.fact: The Interior Ministry's permanent secretary says fines, taxes and duties will be paid by an electronic e-payment model as other sectors follow the ID project; announced, not in service.
